test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 14 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

1. All pens are sketch-pens.

2. Some sketch-pens are markers.

3. No marker is a drawing.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some drawings are markers.

II. No pen is a drawing.

III. Some sketch-pens are pens.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

solution:
Given Statements:

1. All pens are sketch-pens.

2. Some sketch-pens are markers.

3. No marker is a drawing.

The least possible Venn diagram:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16d5da5e5395cb9513bcfd6f54b48218365e4a700980cc1db5f2749f1fdd689f.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some drawings are markers. - **False **(Because No marker is a drawing given, so Some drawings are not markers)

II. No pen is a drawing. - **False **(There is no direct relation given between pen and drawing, so it can be possible but not definite)

III. Some sketch-pens are pens. - **True **(Because All pens are sketch-pens. So, Some sketch-pens are also pens)

So, Only conclusions III follows.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Only conclusions III follows".**
